narrative: Material PL1__M37BBADC shows regular, near-continuous demand (CV=0.37, 98.97% non-zero days) with no detectable trend over the observation period. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=1.12, range 0.12–6.84 days), making lead-time variability the dominant driver of buffer requirements. An (r,Q) policy is recommended: safety stock of 2,008 units absorbs lead-time uncertainty at 95% service level, and an EOQ-derived order quantity of 7,417 units (well above MOQ=1,395) reduces order frequency from 118 to 22 per year, cutting total annual costs by 54%.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Near-continuous demand (98.97% non-zero) with regular CV=0.37 suits a continuous-review (r,Q) model. The deterministic EOQ balances ordering and holding costs while the reorder point embeds a safety stock sized to the combined demand-and-lead-time sigma, appropriate given unstable lead times.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is 76.7% utilized post-replenishment (9,425 of 12,281 units). No binding constraint at present, but any upward demand surge or safety stock increase could stress the remaining 2,856-unit buffer. Monitor capacity quarterly.
